claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II Orion capsule entered the atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. EDT at 24,000 mph.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft endured a 6-minute communication blackout.
Service module separation occurred at 7:33 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Entry interface occurred at 7:53 p.m. EDT at 400,000 ft on April 10, 2026.
Communication blackout began at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Drogue parachutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Splashdown occurred off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew concluded their nearly 10-day mission.
Recovery teams from the U.S. Navy and NASA, including the USS John P. Murtha, managed the retrieval of the astronauts.
